limits: Comparison of whole-ISS mass to only habitat fabric is not an equivalent comparison.
ISS receives frequent cargo and external operational support; this mission carries its supplies, propulsion and settlement seed.
A cruise farm could reduce stocks, but it requires a complete diet, nutrient accounting, maintenance access and failure reserves.
An inflatable envelope saves structural and packaging mass; floors, pressure-restraint loads, radiation protection, machinery and supplies remain.
A broad flat disc needs pressure ties or compartmentalisation; thin fabric alone cannot carry the pressure loads.
About 5 rpm at the compact outer floor requires adaptation studies, especially with repeated torpor recovery.
No calculation here demonstrates a tonnes-scale antimatter bank or establishes an achievable dry mass.
500 t departure is not interchangeable with 500 t retained or 500 t hardware.
